s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Diffuse poikiloderma on upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
key_facts: Previous treatments included systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and IVIG
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles on nailfold examination
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic photosensitive eruption with systemic and cutaneous manifestations
salient_findings: Photosensitive eruption involving face, neck, trunk, and extremities
Diffuse poikiloderma on upper chest, anterolateral thighs, and extensor arms
Erythematous, flat-topped papules on extensor joints of hands
key_facts: Previous treatments included systemic steroids, hydroxychloroquine, methotrexate, mycophenolate mofetil, cyclosporine, tacrolimus, tofacitinib, rituximab, and IVIG
Violaceous erythema on forehead and midface
Dilated capillary loops, capillary dropout, and ragged cuticles on nailfold examination
Elevated serum IFN-β levels (8 pg/mL, normal ≤2 pg/mL)

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical examination revealed violaceous erythema, diffuse poikiloderma, and nailfold changes, consistent with dermatomyositis, and laboratory tests showed elevated serum IFN-β levels and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies

shortlist.label: Lupus erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including photosensitive eruption and systemic manifestations, are consistent with lupus erythematosus, and laboratory tests showed elevated serum IFN-β levels

shortlist.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including dermatomyositis-like skin changes, myositis, and presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, are consistent with mixed connective tissue disease

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's symptoms, including diffuse poikiloderma and nailfold changes, are consistent with scleroderma, although the presence of anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies is more typical of dermatomyositis

shortlist.label: Polymyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Radiographic evidence of myositis and elevated serum IFN-β levels are consistent with polymyositis, although the presence of skin changes is more typical of dermatomyositis

raw.rationale: The presence of violaceous erythema, poikiloderma, and dilated capillary loops, along with elevated serum IFN-β levels and anti-TIF-1γ autoantibodies, are characteristic of dermatomyositis. The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings are consistent with this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Lupus erythematosus
rejected.why: Lack of specific lupus-related symptoms and laboratory findings, such as a positive ANA test or characteristic renal involvement.

rejected.label: Mixed connective tissue disease
rejected.why: Insufficient evidence of overlapping features of lupus, scleroderma, and polymyositis to support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: Absence of characteristic scleroderma symptoms, such as skin thickening or esophageal involvement.

rejected.label: Polymyositis
rejected.why: Presence of skin manifestations, such as violaceous erythema and poikiloderma, which are more characteristic of dermatomyositis than polymyositis.
